$comment: The link graph of everything this project publishes, and the exposure of every host
it publishes on. Hand-maintained, checked by .claude/gates/site_graph.py.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. index.html:277 links the gallery to the studio, and both
catalogues in bikar describe that as the reciprocal loop closing. It points at
bikar.naqshcoffee.com, which is behind Cloudflare Access — so for every visitor but
the owner it lands on a login wall, while the identical bytes sit public at
bikar-studio.pages.dev and are linked from nowhere. Four crawler runs on 2026-08-02
(linkinator live and offline, linkchecker, a headless-Chrome render) reported that
edge as OK/valid=1. They cannot do otherwise: Cloudflare answers an unauthenticated
request with a login page and HTTP 200, so 'does this URL resolve' is the wrong
question and every tool that asks it returns green.
So this file does not record whether a URL resolves. The repo already settled that:
an 8.4% sample of 737 URLs measured ~11% false alarms against a true dead-link rate
under 1%, and a gate that cries wolf gets switched off. It records what only the repo
knows — which host each edge travels through, and what each host's exposure is — and
the gate checks the edges against the exposures. That is a fact about two checked-in
declarations, with no network and no false-positive mode.
There is no standard to conform to here. An XML sitemap is a flat node list by spec
and may not span hosts; HTML's hierarchical link relations (rel=up/index/contents)
were deleted from the WHATWG spec in 2011 and are consumed by nothing; schema.org
SiteNavigationElement has no properties and no known consumer. The survey behind that
conclusion is docs/research/sitemap-link-graph-survey.md.

why: The exposures below are a MIRROR. bikar is a private repo and is not checked out
when this gate runs, so the values are copied here and the gate cross-checks them
only when BIKAR_DIR happens to point at a real clone. This is the same cross-repo
seam Makefile:141-145 already accepts in as many words: 'Adding a page is two
edits, in two repos, and saying so is cheaper than a cross-repo check that would
have to run a build.' Drift is possible; it is bounded to one field per host, and
the gate says out loud which mode it ran in.

$comment: Edges that travel through a host that is public today but sits on a surface that
also has an Access-protected host — i.e. edges that die the day the exposure is
equalised (task #63). None of them break a build and none turn a test red, which
is the whole reason they are counted here rather than remembered. The gate
recomputes this set and fails if the list disagrees; it is a measured number, not
an estimate.
